name: Just wear makeup theory

lead: Just wear makeup (JWM) is a looksmaxxing idea that makeup is the fastest route to better looks: instead of waiting on surgery or long routines, a man evens his skin, covers blemishes and defines his brows with cosmetics.

Its proponents point to luxury houses launching men's lines and to male models and actors who use makeup. No studies test the theory under that name, though cosmetics are well documented as covering blemishes and evening skin tone.

paras: As described in one looksmax.org thread, the suggested approach is moisturiser plus concealer (eye area and blemishes), foundation for an even complexion, and a brow pencil, with bronzer and lip balm as other neutral products. Mascara, eyeliner, blusher and lipstick are labelled by that poster as more obviously feminine.

Makeup can irritate skin or clog pores in some people, and removal and hygiene matter. Social reactions vary by setting; the same thread shows other members calling it unmasculine while the poster argues the opposite.

angle.text: Makeup changes how skin, eye area and brows appear immediately and washes off. Proponents treat it as a low-commitment alternative or complement to procedures.

lead: Just wear makeup theory (JWM) is a looksmaxxing framework arguing that cosmetics are the simplest way to narrow an appearance gap. A looksmax.org thread presenting it calls makeup the easiest looksmax, noting that Chanel and Tom Ford have men's makeup ranges and that male models use it.[1]

The thread proposes a hierarchy: concealer as the single most useful product for the eye area and blemishes, foundation for an even complexion and some sun protection, and a brow pencil as an effective subtle change. It separates products it considers neutral (foundation, concealer, bronzer, brow pencil, lip balm) from ones it considers feminine (blusher, mascara, eyeliner, eyeshadow, lipstick, gloss).[1]
Wikipedia's overview of male cosmetics describes brand launches from Nivea, Chanel and Tom Ford, YouTube beauty creators, and reports that men use products to cover blemishes.[2]
infobox: Concealer, foundation, brow pencil, bronzer, lip balm

paras: The theory frames cosmetics as an easy fix for the 'gap' between a man's face and his ideal. A looksmax.org post sums it up as why not use the easiest looksmax that models already use.[1] It also argues that men's neglect of self-care reflects traditional masculinity, a view other forum members dispute in replies.[1]

The thread's ordering puts moisturiser first, then concealer for the eye area and blemishes, foundation for a flawless complexion and a brow pencil with a brush. The poster cites Timothee Chalamet as an example of men's makeup done well, contrasted with the more dramatic style of James Charles.[1]
Men's cosmetics have existed since antiquity; they re-emerged commercially with 1930s film and grew after the late 1990s, with major fashion houses entering later.[2]

lore.intro: The concept circulates on looksmax.org as a pragmatic softmax.[1]
